lawyer:
A. F. Hasan Arif, Attorney General and A. J. Mohammad Ali, Additional Attorney General (Md. Abdur Rahman Khan, Deputy Attorney General with them) instructed by Mvi. Md. Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Appellant
Md. Fazlul Karim, Senior Advocate (Nikhil Kumar Shaha, Advocate with him) instructed by Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondents
parties:
The Government of Bangladesh ----- Appellant
Vs.
Md. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Syed J. R. Mudassir Husain C. J:-This appeal, by leave granted on 28-02-1992, at the instance of defendant-Government, is directed against the judgment and order dated 4.3.1998 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 693 of 1991 discharging the Rule. 

 2. This appeal by the defendant-Government arises out of a suit for declaration of title (and also for recovery of possession in part by amendment of plaint) being other class suit No. 593 of 1984 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kendua filed by the respondents, which was concurrently decreed by the Courts below and the same was also affirmed in revision by the impugned judgment of the Single Bench of the High Court Division as aforesaid. 

 3. Plaintiff's case is that admittedly one Kasum. Bhuiyan held the disputed land measuring .09 acres in Chandina Jote right under the Court of Wards on behalf of one Amullya Chandra Roy Chowdury and others. Ex-landlord of the suit Touji. It is stated by the plaintiff-respondents that the said Bhuiyan sold the disputed land to one Abbas Ali by the two registered sale deeds dated 13.5.1948. Subsequently, Abbas Ali sold .04 acres of land to the plaintiff-respondents by registered Kabalas dated 10.10.1959, 13.10.1959 and then Abbas Ali again sold .01/2 acres of land to the plaintiff No. 1 by Kabala dated 27.7.1968, Abbas Ali sold the remaining .02% acres of land to the plaintiff No. 2 wife of plaintiff No. 3 by registered Kabala dated 15.10.1960 and thus the plaintiffs acquired right, title and possession of .09 acres of land. On 29.02.1975 the plaintiffs for the first time came to know that out of the said land .07 acres was recorded in their names while the rest .02 acres was wrongly recorded in the khan khatian of the government. During the pendency of the suit defendant No.2 dispossessed the plaintiff from an area of .1/4 acres of land to the north western corner of the suit land on 10.03.1962, raised a structure thereon. 

 5. The trial Court decreed the suit, against which the appeal was preferred by the Government and this appeal was also dismissed. Against the aforesaid judgment of affirmance, Government preferred revision and the High Court Division discharged the Rule by affirming the decrees of the Courts below. 

 6. Mr. A.F. Hassan Ariff, the learned Attorney General along with Mr. A J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Additional Attorney General, appearing for the government, firstly contended that the trial Court as well as the Court of appeal below having themselves found that the suit land is situated within the bazar area (Shahidpur Bazar) and thereby, both the courts below committed an error of law in passing a decree in respect of the said land declaring title (jote right) of the plaintiffs without taking into consideration the provision of Section 20(2a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1951. It is further contended that the High Court Division equally committed the same error. Lastly it is contended by the learned Counsel for the appellant that the impugned decree was passed without considering the relevant law i.e. E.P. Ordinance No. 12 of 1960 and in such view of the matter the decree as passed in the suit could not legally passed. 

 8. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim, the learned Counsel appearing for the plaintiff-respondents, on the other hand, contended that the Courts below as well as the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division having considered the materials on record concurrently decided the case upon proper assessment of the evidence on record and as such the concurrent finding of the courts below have been concurred with by the High Court Division in its revisional jurisdiction. 

 9. We have heard the learned Counsel of both sides and gone through the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. It appears that the suit land is situated within a bazar area (Shahidpur bazar) and the trial Court as well as the Court of appeal below having themselves found the same, the High Court Division without considering the provision of Section 20(2a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951 which had with effect of excluding hats and bazar from the categorically of retainable lands and it vested in the government with effect from the date of notification in 1956 under Sub-section 2 of Section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and therefore the High Court Division equally committed an error of law in affirming the judgment and decree of the Courts below which resulted in an error in the decision causing failure of justice. 

 10. Having gone through the decisions and we find substance in the argument of Mr. Attorney General and therefore we hold that the suit land being within the periphery of hats and bazar have been vested in the Government in such view of the matter, the findings and decisions arrived at by the High Court Division can not be sustained in law. We therefore hold that the decree in respect of the suit land declaring title (jote right of the plaintiffs) thereto can not be sustained in view of the provision of Section 20 (2a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951. The learned Single Judge having failed to apply his judicial mind misdirected himself in affirming the decrees of the Courts below. Since the suit land is within the Shahidpur bazar, the plaintiffs cannot retain this as his khas land as the same has already vested in the Government with effect from the date of notification 1956 tinder wholesale acquisitions under Section 3(2) of the said Act.
